overview: The St Mawes Ferry crosses the mouth of the Fal from Falmouth to the pretty harbour village of St Mawes, a trip of about 2.8 miles that saves a drive of nearly 30. It runs on classic wooden ferries and is one of Cornwall’s most popular boat trips.
On the way you pass both Pendennis and St Mawes castles, big ships and Falmouth’s working docks, and if you’re lucky you might spot dolphins, seals or even a basking shark.

expect.title: The crossing
expect.text: A short, scenic trip across the Carrick Roads in a classic wooden boat.

expect.title: Castles and ships
expect.text: Pendennis Castle, St Mawes Castle and Falmouth’s docks along the way.

expect.title: Wildlife
expect.text: Dolphins, seals and basking sharks regularly visit the harbour.

goodToKnow.label: When it runs
goodToKnow.text: All year, seven days a week, with up to three crossings an hour in summer and hourly in winter. Every sailing depends on tide and weather.

goodToKnow.label: Where from
goodToKnow.text: Leaves from central Falmouth, close to the town’s shops and galleries.

week.slot: Half a day with St Mawes
week.text: Make it a day: hop across, wander St Mawes, see its castle, have lunch by the harbour and come back in the afternoon. It works in most weathers.

pairWith.why: the harbour village at the other end

tips: Sit outside on the way over if the weather’s kind: the views of the castles and harbour are lovely.
